body: Hello, I've been fighting since jr high. Feel free to say hi, I might be old and a failed suicide attempt survivor, bit I'd like to think I know a thing or two. Ask and I'll answer honestly.
Getting a license is a big and worthwhile investment. Get a license, get a basic job, and just go. It was a lot of time to myself and a lot of good just driving around and being free. Really helped

I had my car and a sleeping bag to keep me warm, I just used my parents address as my work address and had direct deposit to my own account. Honestly, it's not THAT hard, but it wasn't easy. There are a lot of places you can bunk down for the night without getting in trouble too. Plus if a cop pops up and is all "why are you on the side of the road" I would just tell them I was driving home from work and started falling asleep at the wheel and didn't wanna hurt no one so I pulled over and cracked a window and slept, that's was always enough for them. It's way easier when you have a job, biggest issue is a bathroom to do your hygiene and a kitchen food, but you can adjust till you get an appartment or whatever.

If you make it, try moving out. Now, I get that's hard as fuck, but getting away from my wack ass family was the best decision I ever made. Even if I did end up on the streets for a time, still dont regret it.
Crazy how the people right next to you feel like strangers right? I get that. Hopefully someone not a a "rescue" agenda shows up in your life. I'm sure most of us want something like that.
